Abstract
Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) addresses the demands of computation-intensive network services by providing pro-
cessing capabilities at the network’s edge, reducing service latency. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) enhance MEC due
to their ﬂexibility, broad coverage, and reliable wireless communication. This paper investigates task ofﬂoading in a UAV-
assisted MEC system with multiple collaborating UAVs, optimizing task allocation in binary ofﬂoading mode to enhance
system efﬁciency. System performance is evaluated in terms of energy consumption and task delay, while the proposed
framework jointly optimizes UAV trajectory design, binary ofﬂoading, computation resource allocation, and communi-
cation resource management to achieve better resource utilization. To overcome the limitations of traditional heuristic-
based approaches, we propose an innovative Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based task ofﬂoading framework and
conduct a comparative analysis of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient with Distance to Task Location and Capability
Matching (DDPG with DTLCM), Deep Q-Network (DQN), and Q-Learning. Our approach leverages DTLCM to enhance
decision-making, allowing UAVs to assign tasks more intelligently by factoring in both their proximity to the task and their
computational capabilities. Experimental results show that DDPG with DTLCM consistently outperforms both DQN and
Q-Learning, delivering more stable task allocation and better adaptability in dynamic scenarios. While DQN is more
stable than Q-Learning in high-dimensional state spaces, it still suffers from discretization constraints. In contrast, DDPG
with DTLCM beneﬁts from a continuous action space, enabling more ﬂexible and ﬁne-tuned decision-making. These
insights underscore the strength of policy-gradient DRL methods, particularly when augmented with context-aware
mechanisms like DTLCM, in advancing UAV-assisted MEC task scheduling and resource optimization.

1 Introduction
Many emerging network applications require substantial
computational resources and impose stringent latency
constraints. MEC has emerged as a promising paradigm to
address these challenges by bringing computation closer to
end users, thereby reducing service delay and network
congestion. However, conventional MEC implementations
rely on ﬁxed edge nodes, which are limited in coverage and
scalability, making them unsuitable for high-density user
scenarios or sparsely connected environments. To over-
come these limitations, UAVs have been increasingly
integrated into MEC systems, offering ﬂexible deployment,
adaptive coverage, and enhanced computational support
[1, 2].
UAV-assisted MEC systems possess distinct character-
istics compared to traditional terrestrial MEC infrastruc-
tures. The mobility of UAVs allows them to reposition
dynamically, enabling real-time task ofﬂoading optimiza-
tion. However, existing studies primarily focus on single-
UAV task ofﬂoading, which, due to its limited computa-
tional capacity, is only feasible for small-scale applications
[2, 3]. As computational demands continue to rise, a Multi-
UAV-assisted MEC framework becomes essential to pro-
vide scalable, distributed computing resources. Unlike
single-UAV systems, a Multi-UAV architecture introduces
additional complexities, including:
•
UAV trajectory design to prevent collisions and main-
tain efﬁcient coverage,
•
Communication
resource
management
to
ensure
stable transmission efﬁciency, and
•
Collaborative task ofﬂoading to effectively distribute
workloads among UAVs.
Most existing UAV-assisted MEC solutions rely on
partial ofﬂoading, where tasks are divided into smaller
subtasks and allocated dynamically based on available
resources. While this approach provides ﬂexibility in
resource allocation and helps reduce computation delays, it
is not always feasible for indivisible computation tasks [4].
In such cases, binary ofﬂoading, where a task is either fully
processed locally or completely ofﬂoaded to a UAV, offers
a
viable
alternative.
However,
implementing
binary
ofﬂoading transforms the task ofﬂoading problem into a
mixed-integer optimization problem, signiﬁcantly increas-
ing computational complexity. Furthermore, task request
patterns and UAV resource availability are highly dynamic,
making long-term optimization essential for improving
overall system performance [5, 6].
Traditional optimization approaches, including heuristic
and convex optimization methods, often fail to address
these challenges due to their inability to adapt to dynamic
network environments and incomplete future information
[7]. Given recent advancements in AI, DRL has emerged as
a powerful technique for solving long-term decision-mak-
ing problems in wireless communications. DRL algorithms
can learn from historical data, explore dynamic network
conditions, and optimize decision-making strategies over
time[8]. This capability makes DRL particularly suit-
able for UAV-assisted task ofﬂoading, where system
parameters change continuously [9, 10].
To address the above challenges, this paper investigates
task ofﬂoading in collaborative UAV-assisted MEC sys-
tems by incorporating DTLCM and binary ofﬂoading. We
develop an optimization framework that integrates DDPG
to enhance system efﬁciency by reducing task delay and
energy consumption. The main contributions of this work
are summarized as follows:
Task Ofﬂoading Optimization in Multi-UAV Networks:
We propose a novel task ofﬂoading framework that
integrates DTLCM to enhance task allocation efﬁciency
and system adaptability in a dynamic MEC environment.
Joint Optimization of Ofﬂoading and Resource Alloca-
tion: We formulate a mixed-integer programming prob-
lem that jointly optimizes UAV trajectory design, task
ofﬂoading, computation resource allocation, and com-
munication resource management while considering
power constraints and latency restrictions.
Performance Evaluation and Comparison: We conduct
extensive comparative evaluations of our proposed
algorithm against state-of-the-art alternatives, demon-
strating superior task ofﬂoading efﬁciency and overall
system performance.
The rest of this paper is organized as follows: Sect. 2
reviews related work on UAV-assisted MEC task ofﬂoad-
ing and reinforcement learning-based optimization. Sec-
tion 3 presents the system model and problem formulation.
Section 4 introduces the proposed method. Section 5 dis-
cusses simulation results and performance evaluation, and
Sect. 6 concludes the paper.
2 Related work

categorize prior work into four key areas:
2.1 Machine learning and federated learning
in IoT-MEC systems
Recent research has explored various machine learning-
based approaches to enhance IoT and mobile edge com-
puting (MEC) systems, particularly in areas such as device
detection, distributed learning, and federated learning.

2.2 Deep reinforcement learning for UAV-
assisted MEC
Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has emerged as a
promising approach to optimize UAV-assisted MEC net-
works, focusing on task ofﬂoading, resource allocation, and
trajectory optimization. Research has demonstrated that
DRL-based algorithms signiﬁcantly enhance Multi-UAV
performance in applications such as cooperative target
search and coverage [14]. The DNQMIX algorithm has
been proposed to improve Multi-agent collaboration for
dynamic UAV search missions [15]. Meanwhile, joint
optimization methods leveraging DRL techniques, such as
deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), have been
applied for resource allocation and trajectory planning,
leading to improvements in spectrum efﬁciency and com-
putational
performance
[16].

ofﬂoading approaches have been introduced to ensure QoS-
driven resource allocation under constrained environments
[18]. While these techniques have shown promising results,
further research is required to enhance their adaptability in
dynamic and large-scale UAV-MEC networks.
2.3 Task offloading and resource management
in UAV-MEC
Task ofﬂoading in UAV-assisted MEC involves optimizing
the distribution of computational tasks between terrestrial
and aerial edge nodes to improve efﬁciency. Several
studies have explored hybrid UAV deployment and task-
ofﬂoading strategies, focusing on minimizing energy con-
sumption while maximizing resource utilization [19].
Intelligent task ofﬂoading methods based on federated deep
reinforcement learning have been introduced to enhance
system reliability and security while mitigating cyber
threats such as trigger-less backdoor attacks [20]. Meta-
heuristic-based and priority-driven DRL approaches have
also been proposed to improve computation ofﬂoading,
reducing latency and increasing resource allocation efﬁ-
ciency in UAV-assisted MEC systems [21]. Furthermore,
service satisfaction-oriented task scheduling models have
been studied to balance job priorities while optimizing
energy efﬁciency [22]. UAV-enabled Multi-hop edge
computing frameworks have been developed to enhance
distributed processing, leveraging DRL algorithms to
maximize task execution success rates [23]. The integration
of decentralized Multi-agent DRL has further advanced
UAV

ofﬂoading
by
improving
resource allocation, task execution efﬁciency, and UAV
mobility in cooperative IoT networks [24]. Despite these
advancements, designing scalable and adaptive task-of-
ﬂoading strategies remains a crucial research direction.
2.4 Optimization strategies for UAV trajectory
and energy efficiency
Optimizing UAV trajectory planning and energy con-
sumption is essential for enhancing MEC system efﬁ-
ciency. Recent studies have explored priority-based DRL
models for energy-efﬁcient UAV path planning, commu-
nication scheduling, and task execution in MEC environ-
ments [25]. DDPG-based approaches have been applied to
optimize UAV-assisted task ofﬂoading by considering task
characteristics, UAV capabilities, and the communication
environment, thereby increasing efﬁciency and reducing
delay [26]. Multi-tier UAV-aided MEC systems have been
studied for their potential to improve load balancing,
resource allocation, and task-ofﬂoading strategies, ensuring
seamless operations under dynamic network conditions
[27]. However, achieving a balance between trajectory
optimization, energy constraints, and computational efﬁ-
ciency remains a signiﬁcant challenge that requires further
investigation. We compare studies related to UAV-assisted
MEC in Table 1. Some authors utilized single UAV-as-
sisted MEC to enhance energy efﬁciency, but this approach
neglected the improvement of delay time. Conversely, the

simultaneously enhance delay time and energy efﬁciency.
In the context of multiple UAV-assisted MECs, we observe
that the degree of improvement varies depending on the

3.4 Task classification model
Tasks in UAVs are categorized based on a combination of
two metrics: distance to the task location and capability
Match.
3.4.1 Distance to task location (DTL)
This metric employs the Euclidean distance formula to
calculate the spatial distance between each UAV and the
task location. Let Di represent the distance of the UAV to
the task location. To normalize this distance, it is divided
by the maximum allowable distance within the operational
area, denoted as Dmax.

4.4 DQN Algorithm
DQN is a value-based reinforcement learning method used
in UAV task ofﬂoading. It is effective for discrete action
spaces but has limitations in handling continuous opti-
mization problems like UAV trajectory planning. There-
fore, we focus on DDPG for better adaptability [37, 38].
Unlike conventional RL-based task ofﬂoading methods
that primarily focus on minimizing latency or energy
consumption, our approach introduces a novel integration
of DTLCM into the decision-making process. By incor-
porating both spatial proximity and computational capac-
ity, our framework ensures more intelligent and adaptive
task allocation. Existing RL approaches such as Q-Learn-
ing and DQN face fundamental limitations in multi-UAV
MEC environments [39, 40]. Q-Learning, being a table-
based method, becomes inefﬁcient as the state space grows,
making it unsuitable for dynamic UAV task scheduling.
While DQN improves upon this by using deep neural
networks, it still suffers from discrete action space con-
straints, limiting the granularity of task assignment deci-
sions. In contrast, our proposed DDPG-based framework
leverages a continuous action space, enabling UAVs to
make ﬁne-grained task allocation decisions based on real-
time system dynamics. This ﬂexibility allows for improved
adaptability in dynamic MEC environments [38, 41].
Furthermore, we redeﬁne the state representation and
reward function by integrating DTLCM, ensuring that
UAVs are assigned tasks based on both location efﬁciency
and computational ability. This novel combination allows
the system to balance task execution load dynamically
while minimizing communication and processing delays,
which is not addressed in prior RL-based ofﬂoading
strategies.

plays a critical role in improving task ofﬂoading efﬁciency
by ensuring a better match between UAV capabilities and
task requirements while minimizing latency. As the number
of UDs increases, resource contention intensiﬁes, leading to
a decline in performance for all approaches; however,
DDPG-DTLCM exhibits superior adaptability, maintaining
signiﬁcantly higher system gain compared to baseline
methods. These ﬁndings highlight the importance of intel-
ligent task allocation strategies and reinforce the potential of
deep reinforcement learning in enhancing the scalability and
efﬁciency of UAV-assisted edge computing networks.
6 Conclusion
This study demonstrates that integrating DTLCM signiﬁ-
cantly enhances UAV-assisted task ofﬂoading efﬁciency,
minimizing task delays and energy consumption. By
coordinating
multiple
UAVs
to
manage
paths,
task
assignments, and resource allocations, DTLCM optimizes
system performance in several ways. It ensures that tasks
are assigned to UAVs that are both geographically closer
and more computationally capable, reducing delays, con-
serving energy, and balancing resource utilization to pre-
vent bottlenecks. Moreover, DTLCM is highly adaptive to
dynamic network conditions, maintaining robust perfor-
mance even as user demands ﬂuctuate.
To effectively address this optimization challenge, we
model the problem as a MDP and introduce a novel DRL
algorithm, DDPG-DTLCM. Extensive experimental eval-
uations conﬁrm that DDPG-DTLCM consistently outper-
forms traditional methods such as DQN and Q-Learning,
achieving
superior
system
gain,
lower
latency,
and
improved resource efﬁciency. The results highlight the
pivotal role of DTLCM in real-time UAV-assisted edge
computing applications, where scalability, responsiveness,
and energy efﬁciency are critical. Future work will explore
further optimizations, including hybrid learning approaches
and real-world deployment scenarios, to further enhance
the
applicability
of
DTLCM
in
large-scale
MEC
environments.

Abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) addresses the demands of computation-intensive network services by providing pro- cessing capabilities at the network’s edge, reducing service latency. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) enhance MEC due to their ﬂexibility, broad coverage, and reliable wireless communication. This paper investigates task ofﬂoading in a UAV- assisted MEC system with multiple collaborating UAVs, optimizing task allocation in binary ofﬂoading mode to enhance system efﬁciency. System performance is evaluated in terms of energy consumption and task delay, while the proposed framework jointly optimizes UAV trajectory design, binary ofﬂoading, computation resource allocation, and communi- cation resource management to achieve better resource utilization. To overcome the limitations of traditional heuristic- based approaches, we propose an innovative Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based task ofﬂoading framework and conduct a comparative analysis of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient with Distance to Task Location and Capability Matching (DDPG with DTLCM), Deep Q-Network (DQN), and Q-Learning. Our approach leverages DTLCM to enhance decision-making, allowing UAVs to assign tasks more intelligently by factoring in both their proximity to the task and their computational capabilities. Experimental results show that DDPG with DTLCM consistently outperforms both DQN and Q-Learning, delivering more stable task allocation and better adaptability in dynamic scenarios. While DQN is more stable than Q-Learning in high-dimensional state spaces, it still suffers from discretization constraints. In contrast, DDPG with DTLCM beneﬁts from a continuous action space, enabling more ﬂexible and ﬁne-tuned decision-making. These insights underscore the strength of policy-gradient DRL methods, particularly when augmented with context-aware mechanisms like DTLCM, in advancing UAV-assisted MEC task scheduling and resource optimization.
